They bring an indie-pop/rock performance with deep soulful lyrics and an uplifting sound, focused on silver linings, seeing the brighter side of life, and reminding audiences that every voice matters. 
 THE YAZ BAND formed in London, with roots in Canada and India. Inspired by Coldplay, Young the Giant, KALEO and Kodaline, their indie pop/rock sound blends atmospheric melodies with deeply reflective lyrics, centred around resilience, perspective and personal growth. description:
What happens when a piece of music moves you - only to realise it was created by AI in seconds? In this performative talk, Denira Coleman and Aritra (Ari) Sutradhar challenge our assumptions about creativity by taking us from ancient ragas and operatic scores to algorithms. Rather than framing AI as a threat, they suggest it may become a collaborator: pushing us to rethink creativity, experience, and meaning in a rapidly evolving world.  Aritra Sutradhar, spent most of his career building at the intersection of creativity, technology, and business.

He began in education strategy, designing higher education programmes across India and Africa, before moving into enterprise technology, working across the Founder’s Office, brand, and product roles at a Data & AI company headquartered in Singapore.

Alongside this, music has remained a parallel discipline throughout his life. Trained in Hindustani classical violin and voice, Aritra has engaged with it through multiple lenses — as a compos
title: Will AI Replace Human Creativity?  | Aritra Sutradhar & Denira Coleman | TEDxLondonBusinessSchool

In their minimalistic duo format, Mike and Carlos weave synthpop ideas with classical arrangements, turning rockabilly on its head through intricate live performance and evocative soundscapes.  The Dandelion Chain is a Hampshire-based post-punk fusion of alt rock and electronic vibes set over dark lyrical harmonies. Their music is an eclectic mix of genres spanning gothic moodiness, indie-pop bangers and anthemic ballads. 

The full band includes:
Mike – Vocals and guitar. 
Lucy – Lead guitar, synth and backing vocals.
Carlos – Bass guitar, Cello and backing vocals.
Matthew – Drums and percussion.

Mike and Carlos performed at TEDxLondonBusinessSchool.

title: The Dandelion Chain – Live Performance | The Dandelion Chain | TEDxLondonBusinessSchool

author: TEDx Talks
description: What happens to truth when AI reshapes the information environment during elections and moments of crisis? From deepfakes to AI chatbots spreading conspiracy theories, technology is increasingly capable of sowing confusion and distorting public perception. This talk challenges you to reconsider the role AI should play in protecting democratic stability, and how it can build resilience rather than erode trust.  Sam Stockwell is Senior Research Associate at the Centre for Emerging Technology and Security (CETaS) within the Alan Turing Institute. His research focuses on how AI is affecting the online information ecosystem, particularly in relation to mis/disinformation, moderating harmful content, and election interference. He also conducts research on challenging issues at the intersection of privacy and safety trade-offs, such as the use of biometrics in law enforcement and lawful access proposals for criminal investigations on end-to-end encrypted networks. This talk was given at a TE
title: AI & information integrity: Seeing is no longer believing | Sam Stockwell | TEDxLondonBusinessSchool

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Chris Caldwell challenges the metrics that have shaped how civilization measures progress, and why those same metrics may be holding us back from solving the climate crisis. Drawing on his work helping to grow Northern Ireland's renewable energy industry, he makes the case that tackling climate change isn't just a technological or political challenge, but a question of what we choose to count as success. A personal turning point first opened his eyes, and now he's asking whether the world is making the same mistake on a much bigger scale.  Chris Caldwell is a renewable energy entrepreneur, clean tech investor, and climate communicator exploring how finance, technology, and leadership shape our climate future. 

An MBA graduate of London Business School, he left investment banking to build renewable energy projects from the ground up. As CEO of United Renewables and related ventures, his teams have delivered more than 40 clean energy projects across wind, solar, hydro, and anaerobic di
title: How we tackle the climate crisis | Chris Caldwell | TEDxLondonBusinessSchool

author: TEDx Talks
description: AI is reshaping medicine, but what if it’s learning from a system that has historically overlooked half the population? This talk exposes how data gaps in women’s health risk being hard-coded into the future of healthcare. Lily is currently pursuing her MBA at London Business School and brings experience across healthcare consulting, product management, and entrepreneurship. Prior to LBS, she worked at Boston Consulting Group, focusing on digital transformation and AI in healthcare, and held roles at early-stage startups across the US and China. Beyond work, she is passionate about expanding access to healthcare through technology, and is actively involved in student leadership at LBS. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The cost of being invisible in medical research | Lily Crawford | TEDxLondonBusinessSchool

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Professor Sir Andrew Likierman explores why good judgment is the essential difference between success and failure, yet remains a skill that is rarely formally taught. He further states that in an era of AI, human judgment becomes even more critical for framing the right questions and interpreting the answers machines provide.  Professor Sir Andrew Likierman is Professor of Management Practice at the London Business School (LBS) and was its Dean from 2008 to 2017.  His current research is in judgment in management, and he has published on judgment in leadership, in professions, on Boards and in the world of AI.  His book “Judgement at work: Making better choices” was published in 2025 (paperback 2026).  

Andrew spent 11 years in the Treasury (the UK Finance Ministry) as Head of the Government Financial Service and before that advised House of Commons Select Committees on public spending.  He has been a member of many public enquiries, including the Cadbury Committee on corporate gover
title: Good Judgment: Here’s How  | Professor Sir Andrew Likierman | TEDxLondonBusinessSchool

Since the first lab-grown burger showcased in 2013, the cellular agriculture field has exploded globally, with scientists and startups all over the world working on the future of food with cellular agriculture. However, after years of rapid investment and excitement, the industry is currently navigating a difficult phase – what many describe as an 'investment winter.' Drawing from his research, Ahmed Khan's talk explores how strategic partnerships across industries may help cultivated meat startups continue building toward long-term impact.  Ahmed Khan is a cellular agriculture consultant and the founder of CellAgri, a news and market insights startup focusing on the future of food with cellular agriculture. 

Having tracked the cellular agriculture field for over 8 years, CellAgri provides the latest updates and insights on a range of topics and trends in the industry. CellAgri’s platform also tracks all the major and upcoming players in the field and shares our insights regularly th
title: The winter before spring: The cultivated meat story | Ahmed Khan | TEDxLondonBusinessSchool

author: TEDx Talks
description:
From surviving domestic violence as a child to advising on presidential campaigns and speaking at the UN, Emmy Coffey Nguyen has spent her life observing and studying this invisible force called power and how most of us are sent into the world completely unprepared for how it really works.
In this talk, Emmy challenges the idea that power belongs only to those with titles or armies. Drawing on Gandhi, Robert Greene's The 48 Laws of Power and her grandmother's journey as a Vietnamese refugee fleeing Saigon, she reveals how power shapes who gets heard, who gets ignored  and who gets left behind, often through generations.
Whether you've felt powerless in a meeting room, a relationship or a system that wasn't built for you this talk is for you.
What you'll take away:
⦁ How personal, relational and political power show up in everyday life 
⦁ Why competence alone won't protect you from power dynamics 
⦁ How to move from pain to power no matter your resources or background Emmy Coffey Nguye
title: Turning Power Games into Power Moves | Emmy Coffey Nguyen | TEDxTUDublin

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Growing up with asthma, struggling to keep up, and never being labeled a “natural talent,” I was far from the image of a future Olympian. In this talk, I share the reality behind elite performance and the struggles that go with it, from my diagnosis as a child, not getting my first Irish vest until I was 21 and why I kept going. My journey to becoming an Olympian was built quietly through resilience, consistency, and self-belief rather than early success or extraordinary talent. I hope to inspire people to explore what happens when you stop chasing instant results and start falling in love with the process.
 Sophie Becker is a 400m and relay athlete who has represented Ireland at two consecutive Olympic Games. A three-time National Champion and European medallist, she is one of Ireland’s foremost sprinters.Alongside her athletic career, Sophie holds a degree in Genetics and Cell Biology and works in pharmaceutical research, giving her a unique ability to combine practical performance
title: From asthmatic kid to Olympian | Sophie Becker | TEDxTUDublin

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A deeply personal talk about fear, identity and the cost of waiting. Through his own experience as an athlete born with one arm and no legs, Colin Judge explores how exactly fear holds us back.

“An Unfinished Future”challenges the idea that we must feel fully prepared before taking action and argues that growth begins the moment we stop playing it small and start contributing, however imperfect that may be.
 Colin Judge is a Paralympic table tennis player, speaker, and actuary who has defied the odds despite being born with no legs and one arm. Although he had a happy childhood, he struggled with confidence during his teenage years and hit a low point. Determined to change, he found table tennis, which transformed his life. He began to accept himself and quickly excelled, making his international debut within four years. He studied Actuarial and Financial Studies at UCD, graduated with a 2:1 degree, and worked at KPMG before taking a sabbatical in 2019 to pursue his Paralympic dream.
title: How to embrace your unfinished future | Colin Judge | TEDxTUDublin

description: True confidence originates from your roots, shown in how you present yourself, the standards you keep, the abilities you've honed, but ultimately, confidence is knowing who you are and spreading kindness. A partir de su experiencia en el estudio MamiMale y del proyecto “Antártica”, un cortometraje en stop-motion, reflexiona sobre arte, territorio y género, cuestionando la ausencia histórica de las mujeres en los relatos sobre el continente blanco y relevando la importancia de crear referentes que inspiren a nuevas generaciones. Ximena Araya Gutiérrez is a Chilean writer, producer and university professor who builds powerful stories through sound, image and animation. Sound engineer trained at EICTV Cuba and Master in Screenwriting at Universidad Finis Terrae, she has led women-centered projects as co-founder and director of Mami Male, a studio dedicated to audiovisual and narrative creations. She has produced award-winning animated content in Chile, coordinated international missions for “Chilean Animation”, and taught executive produc
title: Describe tu aldea y serás universal | Ximena Araya | TEDxPunta Arenas

author: TEDx Talks
description:
En esta charla de TEDx Punta Arenas, Rodrigo Jordán comparte el origen de una vocación marcada por la curiosidad, la montaña y el deseo profundo de transformarse en explorador. Ese anhelo lo llevó  hasta algunos de los territorios más extremos del planeta, entre ellos la Antártica, donde entre 2002 y 2003 integró una expedición chilena que recorrió cerca de 400 kilómetros por la vertiente este de los montes Ellsworth, una de las zonas montañosas más altas y remotas del continente blanco.
A través de esta experiencia, realizada durante 54 días, sin soporte externo, cruzando glaciares, pasos de montaña y enfrentando condiciones límite, Jordán nos invita a mirar la exploración no solo como una hazaña física, sino como una forma de aprender, colaborar y ampliar los límites de lo posible. Rodrigo Jordán is one of Chile’s most prominent explorers, mountaineers, and leadership speakers, internationally recognized for leading expeditions to Mount Everest and other extreme environments. With a
title: Historia de una expedición Antártica | Rodrigo Jordán | TEDxPunta Arenas

author: TEDx Talks
description:
En esta charla de TEDx Punta Arenas, Iván Lara nos transporta a diciembre de 1967, a la Isla Decepción, en la Antártica, para relatar la erupción volcánica que destruyó la base chilena Pedro Aguirre Cerda y el rescate que permitió salvar a quienes se encontraban en la isla.

A través de una crónica histórica y personal, Lara recuerda la acción del buque Piloto Pardo y de su tripulación, que acudieron en auxilio de chilenos, británicos y argentinos en condiciones extremas. Su testimonio es una invitación a preservar la memoria de los pioneros antárticos y a reconocer la solidaridad, el profesionalismo y la valentía que marcaron este episodio de la historia antártica chilena. Iván Lara is a telecommunications specialist whose professional trajectory intersects with one of Antarctica’s most critical historical emergencies. As a direct witness to the 1967 volcanic eruption on Deception Island, he experienced firsthand the evacuation of Chilean bases under extreme conditions, where communi
title: Un nuevo rescate | Iván Lara | TEDxPunta Arenas

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this **TEDx Punta Arenas** talk, researcher **Beatrix Schlarb-Ridley** explores the climate crisis through the lens of Antarctic science. From ice cores that preserve up to 800,000 years of Earth’s history to the loss of sea ice and its effect on the planet’s capacity to reflect sunlight, she shows how Antarctica helps us understand the scale and urgency of global warming.

But her message goes beyond evidence and warning. Schlarb-Ridley invites us to rethink how we communicate climate change, moving away from fear, guilt, and paralysis toward active hope, personal values, and constructive action. Her talk is a call to transform climate anxiety into motivation, and to see Antarctica not only as a place that reveals the crisis, but also as a source of cooperation, innovation, and possibility.
 Beatrix Schlarb-Ridley is Director of Innovation and Impact at the British Antarctic Survey, where she leads efforts to turn polar science into real‑world solutions for climate and society. Wi
title: Unprecedented Climate Change: A Polar Call to Action | Beatrix Schlarb-Ridley | TEDxPunta Arenas

author: TEDx Talks
description:
El oceanógrafo Osvaldo Ulloa nos invita a explorar uno de los territorios menos conocidos del planeta: las profundidades del océano. A través de su experiencia en la Fosa de Atacama, frente a las costas de Chile y Perú, Ulloa revela cómo este lugar de más de 8.000 metros de profundidad desafía nuestra comprensión sobre la vida, la ciencia y los límites de la exploración humana.
Su relato conecta la aventura científica de la expedición Atacamex, el uso de tecnología de vanguardia y el descenso histórico al fondo marino, con una reflexión mayor sobre el valor del océano como patrimonio natural de Chile y laboratorio único para el mundo. Nos invita a mirar el mar con curiosidad, respeto y sentido de futuro, entendiendo que sus profundidades aún guardan respuestas fundamentales sobre la vida en la Tierra.
 Is a leading Chilean oceanographer and a global reference in the study of microbial life in extreme ocean environments. As Director of the Millennium Institute of Oceanography and profe
title: El océano profundo: viaje al último territorio inexplorado | Osvaldo Ulloa | TEDxPunta Arenas

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Phillipe Tortell compara el Ártico y la Antártica desde una mirada científica centrada en el océano, el clima y la vida marina. A través de factores como la circulación oceánica, los vientos antárticos, la temperatura estival y la descarga de agua dulce, muestra que ambos polos funcionan de manera muy distinta: el Ártico presenta una estratificación oceánica fuerte, mientras que la Antártica mantiene una estratificación más débil. Esta estratificación regula la vida marina, al controlar la relación entre luz, nutrientes y productividad biológica. 
También incorpora una dimensión humana, contrastando la población permanente del Ártico con los visitantes antárticos, y destaca el valor de nuevas plataformas científicas, datos automatizados y diversas perspectivas polares para comprender mejor el cambio climático.
 Dr. Philippe Tortell is a Professor of Oceanography and Botany at the University of British Columbia and a leading marine biogeochemistry expert specializing in polar ocean sci
title: Los dos polos de nuestro planeta | Philippe Tortell | TEDxPunta Arenas

author: TEDx Talks
description:
El investigador Marcelo Gutiérrez nos propone un viaje a la Antártica a través de los sentidos y la ciencia. Desde la oceanografía, muestra cómo las aguas antárticas cambian en temperatura, salinidad y oxígeno, y cómo esos procesos, muchas veces invisibles, sostienen la vida marina desde su escala más microscópica, especialmente a través del fitoplancton y el microplancton. Pero también nos muestra como a través del proyectp  Corriente Sonora, los datos oceanográficos son transformados en sonidos, ritmos, colores y movimientos para que el océano pueda ser visto, escuchado y sentido. Creando una experiencia poética, interactiva y reflexiva, donde los datos dejan de ser abstractos y se convierten en una forma de conexión emocional con el océano. 
 Marcelo Gutiérrez Astete es oceanógrafo, académico de la Universidad de Concepción e investigador principal de COPAS Coastal. Es profesor asociado de la Facultad de Ciencias Naturales y Oceanográficas de la UdeC desde 2013 y Principal Investig
title: Corriente Sonora | Marcelo Gutierrez | TEDxPunta Arenas

author: TEDx Talks
description: Leyla reflexiona sobre la Antártica como un territorio que, aunque geográficamente lejano para muchas personas, forma parte del patrimonio común de la humanidad y cumple un rol fundamental en el equilibrio ambiental del planeta. A través de su mirada, plantea que los efectos del cambio climático están generando transformaciones cada vez más visibles en sus ecosistemas marinos, afectando la biodiversidad, las cadenas tróficas y las condiciones naturales que sostienen la vida en este continente extremo. Su mensaje invita a reconocer la importancia de proteger la Antártica, la necesitamos y ella a nosotros. Los cambios que ocurren allí tienen consecuencias que trascienden sus fronteras. Leyla Cárdenas Tavié is a marine biologist and Dean of the Faculty of Sciences at the Universidad Austral de Chile, director of the South-Sub-Antarctic Science Consortium 2023, and coordinator of the Antarctic Natural Laboratory node. With dual PhDs in Biological Sciences with emphasis in Ecology (Pontifi
title: ¿Es la  Antártica realmente Prístina? | Leyla Cardenas | TEDxPunta Arenas

description: For many people, basketball is about competition, discipline, or athleticism. But for Jorge, the game became something far more personal. In this reflective and heartfelt talk, Jorge explores how basketball transformed the way he connects with others, teaching him presence, trust, patience, and communication both on and off the court. Through stories of teamwork, mistakes, and personal growth, he reveals how the lessons learned in sports can quietly shape the relationships that matter most in our everyday lives. Jorge Sabater is an 11th grade student at Nido de Águilas who is passionate about basketball, teamwork, and personal growth. Through his experiences on the court, Jorge has developed a deeper understanding of communication, presence, and the importance of meaningful human connection. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description: What happens when you suddenly become aware of how the world sees you? In this vulnerable and deeply reflective talk, Rori shares her experience of moving across countries and arriving in Chile, where for the first time, her identity as a Black girl became something she constantly noticed. Through moments both subtle and powerful, she explores the invisible ways assumptions, perception, and social expectations can shape how we act, speak, and see ourselves. More than a story about race, this talk is a universal reflection on identity, belonging, and the quiet pressure of being perceived before truly being known. Rori is an 10th grade student at Nido de Águilas whose international upbringing has shaped her perspective on race, identity, and belonging. Through personal storytelling, she explores how moving between cultures changes the way people see themselves—and the way they are seen by others. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organ

Andres explores the pressure to fit into labels and the fear of not fully belonging anywhere. Ultimately, his talk challenges audiences to rethink identity, not as a single place or nationality, but as the collection of experiences, memories, and people that shape who we become. Andres Mejia is an 11th grade student at Nido de Águilas whose international upbringing across the United States, Colombia, Singapore, and Chile has shaped his perspective on identity, culture, and belonging. Through storytelling and personal reflection, Andres explores what it means to grow up between cultures and how those experiences shape the way we understand ourselves. description: In a world built to capture our attention, 11th grade student Roberto Villavicencio explores why boredom may be one of the most important, and most overlooked, parts of human creativity. Drawing from personal stories, neuroscience, and modern digital culture, Roberto examines how constant entertainment and screen time are reshaping the way young people think, imagine, and discover their passions. Through a reflection on curiosity, attention, and the value of empty moments, this talk challenges audiences to rethink boredom not as wasted time, but as the starting point for creativity and self-discovery. Roberto Villavicencio is an 11th grade student at Nido de Águilas originally from Chile. Passionate about curiosity, learning, and reflection, Roberto explores how everyday experiences shape the way young people think, create, and connect with the world around them. After the witnessing both his parents lose their childhood homes through sales and demolitions, Isaac became aware of the grief that we often feel for the places we lose. Through family stories and the perspectives of human geographers, Isaac's talk invites his audience to recognize the significance of the relationships we have with the places around us.
